thread:
sarah: Quick sync — customer (FinEdge) wants a Private deployment but insists on a single shared VPC in their transit account to simplify routing. They're asking for our recommended pattern (PrivateLink vs VPC peering + edge proxy), what firewall rules they need, and an estimate for NAT/EIP pricing.
jamie: Clarify: when you say single shared VPC, do they want our connectors deployed into that VPC or just an egress/bastion?
sarah: They want our connector + edge proxy inside that shared VPC so multiple app accounts can reach it via VPC peering/transit. Their security team prefers not to manage many endpoints.
rohit: That's doable but two big tradeoffs: 1) cross-account peering vs PrivateLink (ENI/VPCE) for each spoke, and 2) whether source IP must be preserved. If they need srcip preserved we should use a NAT in the shared VPC with elastic IPs or a proxy that preserves x-forwarded-for.
mina: Security note: the customer's compliance requires explicit outbound egress IPs for allowlisting and TLS inspection is performed at their perimeter. Do we need any special cert/mtls changes?
jamie: From product side, we support both patterns. PrivateLink (Interface VPCE) keeps spokes from creating routes to our subnets but needs one VPCE per spoke/subnet — can be heavy to operate. Peering/transit allows fewer endpoints but more routing management and potential asymmetric routing if they have inspection.
alex: Also call out pricing: PrivateLink has per-VPCE hourly + data processing. NAT/EIP has egress data transfer + NAT gateway hourly. For a POC with ~1TB/month, estimate rough numbers: NAT GW + EIP ~= $80-150/mo + egress charges; PrivateLink per endpoint can be $0.01/hr + data processing. I'll pull exact region figures if wanted.
sarah: They also asked for a minimal firewall allowlist we can provide to their network team so they can pre-approve before the POC. Can we draft that?
rohit: Minimal allowlist for Private mode (connector in shared VPC + egress via NAT):
```
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to: 34.200.10.0/24, 52.45.120.0/24 (example service EIPs)
- DNS egress UDP 53 to corporate resolvers or 8.8.8.8 (if allowed)
- Allow management SSH from ops bastion IPs (if required)
- If using PrivateLink: allow HTTPS to vpce-*.amazonaws.com domains over 443
```
rohit: Note: those IP ranges are placeholders — we'll provide authoritative EIP list once region selected. Use FQDNs where possible: api.redwood-inference.com, uploads.redwood-inference.com
mina: For security questionnaire — they asked about TLS cert validation and mutual TLS. Our connector supports TLS 1.2/1.3 and can be configured with client certs for mutual auth. We should document the config path and rotation expectations.
jamie: Operational ask: for canary/fallbacks we recommend route-based failover to a secondary region or a small dedicated capacity pool. If they deploy single-VPC, they lose some isolation between tenants — call that out.
sarah: Great. Can someone produce a concise one-pager (network diagram + firewall snippet + cost bullets) we can send to the customer's network/security? POC timeline aims to start next week.
alex: I'll draft the one-pager. @rohit can you confirm whether we should recommend PrivateLink or peering given they mentioned TLS inspect?
rohit: If TLS inspect sits inline and breaks SNI, peering + NAT in shared VPC is simpler because the traffic path is under their control. PrivateLink can complicate inspection since VPCE terminates TLS to the endpoint. Recommend peering/transit for their scenario.
mina: Also add an item: key management — if they plan to use customer KMS for any secrets we need KMS key ARN + IAM cross-account policy.
sarah: Perfect. I'll capture that in the handoff.
deploy-bot: Deployment checklist created: PRD-4579 (private-deploy/finedge) — status: draft.
jamie: Quick checklist for the customer message: 1) confirm region and expected monthly egress; 2) decide on srcip preservation requirement; 3) provide ops bastion IPs for management allowlist; 4) confirm whether they want mutual TLS.
sarah: I'll send that list and cc this thread. Thanks everyone — please add any other blockers.
rohit: One more: if they want static egress for more than 10 spokes, consider central egress with a pool of EIPs + autoscaling NAT fleet to reduce cost vs per-spoke VPCEs.
mina: And security docs: I'll attach our POC security checklist in the follow-up (SOC2 controls, rotation cadence, audit logs).
sarah: Awesome, closing the loop — will share customer's answers and region tomorrow.
